Figure 2: An example of Theorem 5.2. In the left panel, the red curve represents the amortized value distribution K(κ), and the black curve the shifted prior F (κ + c). In the right panel, the red curves represent the support of the 2-D distribution in the equilibrium. In the light blue and light yellow regions, low values and high values are fully revealed; in the light green region, values are pooled to produce amortized values uniformly distributed on an interval. In particular, values above θ∗ + c and those below are paired in the pooling, where θ∗ ≜ f−1(ρ). In this non-degenerate case, θ′1 = θ2.
